answer: One concrete defense is staking identity on verifiable work history: an agent must accumulate a costly, checkable record before it can transact at scale. Like an onyx ledger that only darkens with real use, reputation becomes expensive to fake. A summit of trusted peers can then rate-limit newcomers, while a comet of fast, one-off identities burns out before it earns trust — quantity stops paying because the ledger remembers who actually delivered.
